This policy explains how SMEmarket collects, uses, shares and protects personal data when you use www.smemarket.ae (the "Site"), whether you are buying a business, selling one, or using our Grow services. It is written to meet the UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (the "PDPL").
SMEmarket is operated by SME Market L.L.C-FZ, a limited liability company formed and licensed in the Meydan Free Zone, Dubai, United Arab Emirates.
Licence number: 2654774.01 (formation number 2654774), issued under the Meydan Free Zone regulations
Registered address: Meydan Grandstand, 6th floor, Meydan Road, Nad Al Sheba, Dubai, UAE

For the purposes of the PDPL, SME Market L.L.C-FZ is the controller of the personal data described in this policy. Article 10 of the PDPL requires a Data Protection Officer only for high-risk processing (because of new technology or the volume of data), for systematic evaluation of sensitive personal data, or for large volumes of sensitive personal data, with the thresholds to be set by the Executive Regulations, which have not yet been issued. Our processing is small in scale, so we have not appointed a formal DPO. Because our buyer identity check uses AI on identity documents, we have carried out a written risk assessment of it (PDPL Article 21) and we review it whenever the check changes. Our privacy contact is admin@smemarket.ae. If the Executive Regulations require us to appoint a DPO, we will do so and publish their contact details here.
Because we are licensed in the Meydan Free Zone (not the DIFC or ADGM), the federal PDPL is the data protection law that applies to us. The DIFC and ADGM data protection laws do not apply.

We collect what we need to run a confidential marketplace: your account details, the identity check needed to sign an NDA, what sellers tell us about their business, and the messages you send through the Site.

When a buyer signs an NDA, the seller of that listing sees the signed NDA so they can decide whether to approve them. Sellers never see a buyer's ID document, nationality or phone number. The seller's identity and confidential business details are shown to a buyer only once the seller has approved them.
All communication between buyers and sellers goes through SMEmarket.
We do not sell your personal data, and we do not use advertising or tracking cookies.
We use a small number of service providers (Cloudflare, xAI, Google and Microsoft), some of which process data outside the UAE.
You can ask to see, correct, export or delete your data at any time by emailing admin@smemarket.ae.

When you sign up we collect your full name, email address and phone number (with any country code). If you choose a password, we store only a salted hash of it (PBKDF2-SHA256); we never store or log your password in plain text. If you sign in with a one-time code, we email the code to you and it expires after a short time.
To unlock a listing's confidential details, a buyer signs a non-disclosure agreement (NDA). As part of this we collect:
a photo of your passport data page, or the front and back of your Emirates ID;
the details read from that document: your name as printed, date of birth, nationality, document type, expiry date and the last 4 characters of the document number (we do not store the full number);
the result of the identity check (passed or flagged, and short reasons), including whether you are 18 or over;
what you enter on the NDA: your name, company (optional), typed and/or drawn signature, budget, source of funding and timeline;
the time you signed, your IP address and your browser's user-agent, the NDA version, so we have a record of the agreement.

If you list a business we collect your answers to the seller questionnaire, which can include the business name, industry, location, asking price, revenue, profit, years trading, number of employees, rent and lease terms, and your reason for selling. You can also upload documents to a private data room, such as the trade licence, financial statements, VAT returns, bank statements, the lease or Ejari, a credit report (AECB), staff records (MOHRE / WPS), MOA or ownership documents, asset lists, contracts and photos. These documents may contain personal data about you and about other people (for example employees or business partners). Please share only what is needed and make sure you are allowed to share it.

We keep the messages you send and receive through the Site's chat, including messages from visitors who are not signed in (identified only by a random guest ID). Some replies may be written by an AI assistant (see section 12).

We keep the listings you save or archive, the NDAs and access requests you make, the enquiries you start (including when you tap a "contact us on WhatsApp" button), and a log of key decisions (for example a seller approving or declining a buyer, or an admin action).

If you use the free growth assessment or ask about our Grow services (SEO, paid ads, SDR/outreach, social media management, the enquiry desk and website redesign), we collect your company name, website address, your answers, and the assessment we produce. To produce it, we look at your public website.
If you email us or message us on WhatsApp, we receive your name, number or email address and what you send.

Like any website, our hosting provider receives your IP address and browser details when you visit. We use IP addresses for security (for example limiting repeated login attempts). We also count page views, listing views and WhatsApp clicks as simple daily totals. These counters do not store IP addresses, user IDs or cookies.
A seller may give us information about other people in their documents.

We do not sell your personal data. We share it only as follows.

Sellers. When a buyer signs an NDA for a listing, the seller who owns that listing can see the request and open the signed NDA, so they can decide whether to approve the buyer. From the moment the NDA is signed, whether or not the seller has approved the buyer yet, the seller can see:
the buyer's name, email address and company (if given);
the type of ID document (passport or Emirates ID);
whether the ID was checked (an "ID checked" or "ID not verified" label; the detailed results and reasons are seen only by SMEmarket);
the buyer's stated budget and timeline;
the buyer's signature, when they signed, and the IP address and browser recorded at signing.

Sellers never see the images of the buyer's passport or Emirates ID, and they cannot open them through any page or link. They also never see the buyer's nationality, date of birth, phone number, source of funding or the detailed results of the identity check. Only the buyer and SMEmarket administrators can see the ID images. Approving the buyer does not give the seller any more of the buyer's details; it opens the full listing to the buyer. A seller can also let SMEmarket approve buyers for them. Sellers must use a buyer's details only to decide on that buyer's request.

Buyers. Public listing cards never show the seller's identity, the business name or the reason for selling. A buyer sees confidential listing details and data room documents only after signing an NDA and being approved by the seller. Seller contact details are not shared; all communication goes through SMEmarket.
Service providers. Companies that host the Site, send emails, run the AI features and store backups for us (see section 6). They act on our instructions.

Professional advisers and authorities. Our lawyers, accountants and auditors where needed, and courts, regulators, the UAE Data Office or law enforcement where the law requires it or to protect our rights.

Our providers store and process data outside the UAE, mainly in the United States and Europe, and Cloudflare caches data in its data centres worldwide. The PDPL allows this. Article 22 allows transfers to countries with adequate data protection laws (for example the EU member states, which have the GDPR). Where a country does not have adequate protection, Article 23 allows the transfer on other grounds, including where it is necessary to perform a contract with you and where the recipient is bound by a contract that protects the data. We rely on:
necessity for our contract with you: we cannot host the Site, send your emails or run the identity check you ask for without these providers;

contractual safeguards: each provider's data processing terms bind it to process data only on our instructions, keep it confidential and secure, and use sub-processors only under equivalent terms. Cloudflare and Google also offer the EU Standard Contractual Clauses;
your consent for the identity check, given when you upload your ID, which includes sending the image to xAI in the United States.
When the PDPL Executive Regulations set more detailed transfer rules, we will follow them and update this section.

No system is completely secure. If a personal data breach affects your privacy, confidentiality or security, we will notify the UAE Data Office (or the authority that takes over its role) and tell you, as required by Article 9 of the PDPL, and explain what we are doing about it.
Under the PDPL (Articles 13 to 18) you have the right to:
Information and access: know what personal data we hold about you, why, who we share it with (inside and outside the UAE), how long we keep it, and how it is protected, free of charge.
Portability: receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format.
Correction: have inaccurate data corrected or incomplete data completed.
Erasure: have your data deleted when it is no longer needed, when you withdraw consent, or when it was processed unlawfully. We may keep some data where the law requires it or to defend legal claims.
Restriction: ask us to limit how we use your data, for example while we check its accuracy.
Stop processing: ask us to stop processing, including for direct marketing.
Object to automated decisions: object to decisions made only by automated processing that affect you, and ask for a person to review them.

To use any of these rights, email admin@smemarket.ae from the address on your account. We may ask you to confirm your identity. We will reply within 30 days of receiving your request. If the PDPL Executive Regulations set a shorter period, we will follow it. You can also edit your profile and delete your listings yourself from your account.
If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, please contact us first. You can also complain to the UAE Data Office (or the authority that takes over its role).

We also use your browser's local storage to save your progress in the seller questionnaire, and session storage to keep the chat window open as you move between pages. These stay on your device. You can block or delete cookies in your browser, but you will not be able to sign in without them.

Identity check. When a buyer uploads a passport or Emirates ID, the image is sent to xAI's Grok vision model, which reads the document and checks whether it looks genuine, is in date, matches the name you typed and shows you are 18 or over. The check does not make the final decision on its own: a doubtful result is only flagged for an SMEmarket administrator to review, and the NDA still goes to the seller. The only automatic outcome is being asked to upload again when the image is clearly not an ID document. You can ask for a person to review any result.

AI chat replies. Replies to buyers in the chat may be written by an AI assistant using xAI's Grok models. The assistant sees only what that buyer is allowed to see (public listing details, or confidential details once approved), never the seller's contact details or documents. It hands over to a person for anything sensitive, and a person can reply at any time. You can ask to talk to a person in the chat.
Growth assessment. Your company name, website and answers are sent to xAI's Grok models to produce the assessment. It is a recommendation only.
None of these produce decisions with legal effect about you without human involvement.
